title: Ops Doorbell: Autoremediation Gateway for Tier-1 Support
creator: Ayesha Rao
description: Problem: Tier-1 engineers receive a high volume of repetitive alerts where safe, deterministic remediation steps exist (restart service, rotate cache, clear prefix). Goal: Ship a lightweight gateway — "Ops Doorbell" — that can translate monitored event patterns into verified runbook-tasks, execute idempotent remediation actions with strong guardrails, and surface structured audit and replay artifacts in the Console. The gateway should integrate with existing runbooks-as-tasks pieces (task serializer, safety manifests) and Redwood Console tracing so we have token-level cost/latency visibility for remediation flows.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Doorbell routes events to a rule engine and produces a runbook-task bundle for >= 80% of chosen alert archetypes.
2) Every auto-remediation action is idempotent and reversible or marked for manual review.
3) RBAC enforced: only service accounts with remediation-role can execute; actions logged to audit trail.
4) Metrics and traces appear in Console; per-action latency and token cost visible.
5) Canary rollout: gate enabled for 10% of alerts in staging, 100% off by default until PM signoff.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight Doorbell service (k8s deployment) consumes alert stream (Kafka), matches against rule-sets (yaml) and emits Runbook Task Bundles (RTB). RTBs are validated against safety-manifests and sent to the Task Executor via existing runbooks-as-tasks API. Key components: rule engine (Lua-based matchers), RTB serializer, safety validator, execution broker, telemetry exporter. Important decisions: use existing task schema to maximize reuse; implement a non-blocking dry-run mode for new rules. Trade-offs: implementing very complex matching language adds developer velocity cost; chosen approach favors simple, observable YAML rules with optional scripting only after manual review. Idempotency model: every action carries an idempotency-token (namespace + alert_id + version). Audit: every step emits structured event to Console; links to traces and PR for the runbook are bundled with the RTB. Security: service uses customer-scoped KMS keys for sensitive ops and requires remediation-role via SSO groups.
progress_updates: 2026-02-11 - Ayesha Rao: Initial scoping complete. Spike showed Kafka consumer + simple YAML matcher can classify ~70% of sample alerts from last 30 days.
2026-02-20 - Ethan Morales: Prototype RTB serializer submitted (PR #4582). Running local end-to-end with task-executor mock. Open items: replayability metadata and trace linking.
2026-02-28 - Security review (C. Patel): requested stronger KMS scoping and an explicit failure-mode where secrets are not accessible; added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-03 - PM review (L. Nguyen): agreed to canary gating strategy and asked for dashboard widgets for remediation success rate per-rule.
2026-03-07 - QA (R. Singh): automated harness for dry-run created; observed one non-idempotent restart flow — converted to safe variant and added compensating action.
2026-03-09 - Engineering: merged PR #4689 implementing safety validator. Beginning staging rollout to 5% of alerts in staging cluster.
2026-03-10 - Observability: initial telemetry shows median remediation latency 320ms and negligible cost delta in token metrics.
test_plan: Unit tests for rule matching and RTB serializer. Integration tests with task-executor in staging. Canary rollout to 5% alerts with dry-run flag for 48h, then 10% with actual exec on non-production namespaces for 72h. Chaos test: simulate duplicate alerts and validate idempotency; simulate KMS failure and verify safe-fail behavior. Postmortem window: 7 days of heightened alerting after each rollout stage.
rollback_plan: Feature flag at gateway layer allows immediate global disable. Task Executor will ignore RTBs signed by Doorbell when rollback applied. Also maintain playbook to manually disable Kafka consumer and revert rule-set to read-only. Track rollbacks in Console with staff+timestamp.
